featured_reviews.name: Abhijeet sonavale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bollywood Tours offers an immersive and exhilarating experience for fans of Indian cinema. Located in the vibrant city of Mumbai, the heart of Bollywood, this tour takes visitors on a behind-the-scenes journey into the glitz, glamour, and magic of the world's largest film industry.

From the moment you embark on the tour, you are transported into the captivating world of Bollywood. Led by knowledgeable guides who are well-versed in the industry, visitors get exclusive access to iconic film studios, sets, and locations where some of Bollywood's most beloved movies have been filmed. It's a rare opportunity to witness firsthand the creativity and craftsmanship that goes into making a blockbuster film.

One of the highlights of the Bollywood Tour is the chance to catch a glimpse of your favorite stars in action. Whether it's spotting a celebrity on set or visiting popular hangout spots where Bollywood royalty frequent, there's always a sense of excitement and anticipation in the air.

But the tour isn't just about star-studded encounters. It also offers valuable insights into the history, culture, and evolution of Bollywood, shedding light on the industry's rich heritage and its impact on Indian society and global pop culture.

In addition to studio visits and star sightings, Bollywood Tours also includes interactive experiences such as dance workshops, where visitors can learn signature Bollywood dance moves, and costume trials, where they can dress up as their favorite Bollywood characters for a memorable photo opportunity.

Overall, Bollywood Tours offers a captivating blend of entertainment, education, and excitement that appeals to fans of all ages. Whether you're a die-hard Bollywood buff or simply curious about the inner workings of the film industry, this tour is sure to leave you star-struck and inspired.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Kapoor
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just wanted to pass along our thoughts on the Bollywood tour as we felt our experience was a little disappointing to say the least for the City + Bollywood Tour.

Starting with the very beginning, the guide was late in the morning. We planned for 9-930 the night before, but he didn't arrive until 10:30am citing traffic as the reason. But as Indians we are all well aware that traffic is the norm in Mumbai and should be planned for accordingly.

A late start means everything was either delayed or rushed as a result. We proceeded with the tour and had to mention each of the viewpoints serving as a reminder whereas I would think it's an expectation that the guide would show us everything without mention. At Taj and Gateway of India we made a short stopover but were wondering that for us it turned out that we had already seen it before but for other tourists how would you expect them to see and enjoy the place in a short rushed time? We then reminded him of Mani Bhawan and other viewpoints, before making our way towards "star homes".

This was definitely the most oversold part of the tour as we saw Shahrukh Khan and Salman's house and Farhan Akhtar. In fact there were other houses on the way that we enquired about to which the guide informed us that it belonged to this celebrity etc, but again I would think this is an expectation, especially when your travellers are Indian. (no kidding, I was able to provide more celebrity addresses on an Ola cab ride) we asked of other houses in Pali Hill and Amitabh's house but it was "out of the way" and also apparently the houses you show depends on where the tour begins which is quite disappointing, a tour should have a proper itinerary.

After the fact, I also reconciled with the word doc and noticed the restaurant we were taken to was Shalimar and not Copperchimney - we were not given an option and once again, this speaks to my point that as the guest I felt like I should have policed the entire route and every fine detail (maybe I should have gotten paid to be the co-pilot). The restaurant was definitely not hygienic as there were fruit flies on pickles and even our drinks but since we were already "late" for the dance we made our way out to SJ. The studio itself is pretty substandard and for serials, yet the guide did a good job to show us around because he was kind enough to arrange us another viewing of another shoot at Filmistaan. At the same time, he emphasized that it was a personal favor though he mentioned the company has relations with studios so they are aware of shoots so not sure if the facts reconciled there and if it really was an additional favor. Such additional favors feel quite burdening so would try and watch the language for guests.

The highlights were the singing studio though again the experience should not feel rushed and feel as if it is not included in the tour but done as a favor. (The guide was kind to ask if any of us sings, but if we said no it would not be a part of the tour... I would expect the tour to be complete as per the itinerary because a traveller would not know what a recording studio experience is like regardless of whether or not they sing).It should be a more organized natural part of the tour as it changes the way one perceives the tour and enjoys it.

All in all, at over $200 per person the tour was not worth the price whatsoever. The car itself was substandard, I'm sure at that cost a newer fresher car can be arranged as it smelled of smoke (cigarette smokes) which is quite disgusting.

featured_reviews.name: Dr Anuradha Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Film Studios: The Heart of Cinematic Magic

Film studios are the creative powerhouses that bring stories to life, turning scripts into immersive visual experiences. These spaces are more than just physical locations—they are hubs of imagination, where directors, actors, and technicians collaborate to craft films that captivate audiences worldwide. From grand soundstages to cutting-edge post-production facilities, film studios play a vital role in shaping the magic of cinema. Whether producing large-scale blockbusters or intimate indie films, these studios provide the foundation for storytelling at its finest, blending artistry with technical brilliance.

Yash Raj Films: A Legacy of Excellence in Indian Cinema

Yash Raj Films (YRF) stands as a pillar of Indian cinema, synonymous with grandeur, romance, and timeless storytelling. Founded by the visionary Yash Chopra, YRF has redefined Bollywood with its unparalleled craftsmanship, producing films that resonate across generations. From heartwarming love stories to gripping thrillers, the studio has consistently set new benchmarks in filmmaking. Beyond its artistic brilliance, YRF has also built an empire with its state-of-the-art studios, fostering talent and innovation. With its keen eye for storytelling and commitment to excellence, Yash Raj Films continues to shape the future of Indian cinema, leaving an indelible mark on audiences worldwide.

भारतीय मूल की पहली पूर्ण लंबाई वाली मोशन फ़िल्म दादा साहब फाल्के द्वारा निर्मित की गई थी, जिन्हें भारतीय सिनेमा का अग्रणी माना जाता है। उन्होंने महाकाव्य राजा हरिश्चंद्र का निर्माण किया था, जो एक मूक फीचर फ़िल्म थी जिसमें सभी पुरुष कलाकार थे क्योंकि उस समय महिलाओं को अभिनय के लिए नहीं माना जाता था। यह फ़िल्म 1913 में रिलीज़ हुई थी।

featured_reviews.name: Kisankumar Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari is located in Goregaon and in common language known as Mumbai Film City.
Many popular movies are shot here including the recently released blockbuster Dhurandhar - the climax scene where hamza is in the car was shot in this film city.

The place is amazing and here they offer tour of the entire city within 2 hours with an amazing bollywood show, 8d show which has immersive experience and various places to take photos and experience filmmaking process.

If you are travelling with family or friends you'll have a good time.

review_photos.caption: Entrance of film city
The famous temple which was a part of many iconic films

featured_reviews.name: pawan parihar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing experience visiting Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari (Film City), Mumbai. 🎬✨
It was exciting to see the real world of Bollywood, huge shooting sets, and beautiful locations surrounded by greenery. The atmosphere feels truly cinematic, and if you’re lucky, you may even spot live shooting or famous actors.
A must-visit place for movie lovers and anyone visiting Mumbai! 🌿🎥

featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Jha
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s very underwhelming. Rupees 1200 for this does not makes sense. I wanted to leave after the first experience but you can’t because there is no way other than their bus which will only take you after your complete trip. After 3.5 hours of wasting my time, I returned with a headache and 1200 less in my wallet.

2 stars because it atleast shows you a few shooting spot. And you should return just after the bus tour through the park.

The management also pays commission to auto and taxi guys and hence they take you there and make up stories about how awesome it is.

featured_reviews.name: Minakshi Puzari
featured_reviews.review_text: They take you on 1 hour bus ride through the location but you can't enter any set. You can only hope to see outdoor shooting. Impossible to see the superstars. Then they have 2 hour show which is average. Good for one time visit and only if you have nothing else to do

featured_reviews.name: darshan rawal
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is a fantastic place for shootings, it may be ads, webseries, daily soaps, movies, album songs, vertical series, etc, etc, etc

Anything you can imagine , you are welcomed to shoot here. For better transportation goverment bus service is available. Also a new flyover bridge is under construction from Oberoi mall to directly film city for avoiding the traffic and the transportation of shooting vehicles and equipments.

featured_reviews.name: Arpit Porwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bollywood Park is a decent place to visit, but not as grand as expected. Most of the film sets are either covered or not accessible, so you only get a glimpse of a few memorable spots like Taarak Mehta ka Ooltah Chasmah sets from far that are ok for quick photos.

The museum section is actually nice for clicking pictures, with well-designed setups and film-themed decor. The live show was the highlight well performed and quite engaging. Overall, it’s good for a one-time visit, especially if you enjoy Bollywood vibes, but don’t go in expecting full studio-style access as ticket price does not justify it.

featured_reviews.name: Mesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
HIGHLIGHT - If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

My recent visit to Mumbai Film City was far from what I had hoped. To start, the nearest metro station is Aarey, it is about 4 km away. From there, take an auto (no more than ₹150) straight to the official ticket counter. Be cautious, several individuals may try to sell you tickets along the way at inflated prices. Avoid them, as they are scammers.

After a long wait, we were taken inside the premises by an AC bus. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming from the beginning. Compared to Hyderabad's Film City, this one feels small, restricted, and poorly organized. Most of what you see are large tin sheets covering the sets, there is no access to the actual sets themselves. It felt like being shown billboards of what you could see, but never actually do.

The tour ends at Bollywood Park, which hosts a few staged performances. This was the only mildly enjoyable part. The on site restaurant is strictly vegetarian, which may not appeal to everyone, and the food was overpriced for its quality.

Overall, Mumbai Film City lacks substance, feels commercialized, and fails to deliver the behind the scenes magic one would expect. If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.
